## 固定收益開盤主論

7月17日美國公債收盤走勢，清楚區分了聯準會近期政策風險與較長天期債券的需求。2年期殖利率上升3.8個基點至4.18%，5年期上升0.9個基點至4.279%；10年期下降0.5個基點至4.549%，30年期下跌1.3個基點至5.071%。曲線前端呈現空頭趨平，2年與10年期利差收窄4.3個基點至36.9個基點，2年與30年期利差則收窄5.1個基點至89.1個基點。

當日走勢並未逆轉美債本週由通膨數據帶動的漲勢。2年期殖利率仍較一週前低2.9個基點，10年期也低1.3個基點，但交易員不願全面追高債券的原因已經浮現。6月進口物價再次上升，克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack表示，持續性通膨是她最主要的顧慮；美國與伊朗再度互相攻擊，進一步干擾荷莫茲海峽航運，也使WTI與布蘭特原油大漲約4.5%。即使交易員大致排除7月升息，這些發展仍保留了年內稍後緊縮的可能性。

當日經濟數據的內部結構好壞不一。住宅開工年率大增19%至142.7萬戶，但增幅集中於多戶住宅，獨棟住宅開工略降，建築許可也下滑。工業生產僅增0.1%，製造業產出持平，產能利用率仍遠低於長期平均。進口物價上升0.3%，較一年前高7.1%，創2022年8月以來最快年增幅，儘管能源對月增率的貢獻已經減弱。

這組合也解釋了為何前端遭到賣壓之際，長端仍能回升。10年期實質殖利率下降1.9個基點至2.295%，與經濟活動數據不均及科技股領跌時出現的長天期債券需求一致。10年期損益兩平通膨率則上升1.4個基點至2.254%，反映新的能源衝擊及非燃料進口成本的持續壓力。因此，10年期名目殖利率小幅下降，是實質利率走低與通膨補償上升相抵後的結果，而非全面反映通膨降溫。

油價與科技股對整體風險資產形成相反壓力。WTI收於每桶$82.49，布蘭特原油收於$88.10，兩者本週均累漲近16%。新的中國AI模型加劇競爭後，投資人開始質疑AI投資循環的經濟效益，Nasdaq 100下跌1.49%、費城半導體指數下跌1.63%，S&P 500下跌1.01%。VIX大漲12.19%至18.77。黃金上漲0.68%至每盎司$4,012.70，但全週仍跌2.23%；美元指數近乎持平。

企業債也日益反映市場對AI投資的重新評估。2025年初以來，四家大型科技公司借款逾$3,000億，使其債券在全球信用指數中占有顯著比重，其中許多債券自發行以來表現落後。這項供給壓力有別於迫切的違約風險：借款人財務實力強健，但反覆進行大型融資，迫使投資人承擔愈來愈高的單一發行人及產業集中度。槓桿融資方面，Cotality提高殖利率、將更多資金轉由貸款籌措並加強債權人保障後，才完成艱難的$52.5億再融資。兩者共同顯示信用資金仍可取得，但融資條件愈來愈取決於槓桿、文件條款，以及各借款人投資論述能否持續成立。

## 美國數據好壞不一，聯準會後續路徑仍保留空間

本週CPI與PPI偏軟之後，6月貿易物價帶來較不利的通膨訊號。進口物價較5月上升0.3%，前月增幅則由原值上修至1.7%；年增率達7.1%，為2022年8月以來最大。出口物價繼5月上升1.2%的修正值後，6月月減0.6%，但12個月增幅仍達10.2%。

進口物價的組成，呈現當前能源成本舒緩與更廣泛成本壓力之間的差異。燃料進口價格在5月大漲12.6%後，6月下降0.4%；其中石油價格下跌0.7%，進口天然氣價格則上升9.2%。非燃料進口物價6月上升0.4%、年增4.2%，代表即使燃料價格不再按月上升，貿易商品通膨仍可能持續傳導。農產品出口價格上升0.2%，非農產品出口價格則下降0.7%。

這些數據並未推翻6月CPI與PPI的有利結果；後兩者已大幅降低市場對7月升息的預期，但進口物價顯示通膨改善並不全面。6月汽油與原油價格下跌，壓低消費者及生產者能源價格，進口物價卻顯示燃料以外的成本壓力仍在。隨後油價反彈，也意味6月有利的燃料月度比較未必能反映7月正在形成的成本環境。

住宅市場同樣呈現分歧。住宅開工總數由5月修正後的119.9萬戶年率，大增19%至經季節調整的142.7萬戶。至少5戶的多戶住宅開工年率達51.3萬戶，貢獻了大部分表面增幅。獨棟住宅開工則下降0.2%至89.5萬戶，幾乎沒有跡象顯示6月通膨下降已緩解建商所稱的負擔能力與融資限制。

前瞻指標較弱。建築許可下降3%至136.7萬戶年率，其中獨棟住宅許可下降2.4%至87.1萬戶。完工量整體增加3.3%至139.2萬戶，獨棟住宅完工量則上升6.6%至96.4萬戶。數據顯示當前施工一度加速、完工住宅供給增加，但未顯示未來住宅建設計畫普遍轉強。

工業生產持續擴張，但未重現數項地區製造業調查所呈現的強勁程度。6月總產出上升0.1%，較一年前增加1.1%；製造業產出持平，礦業及公用事業產出各增0.4%，整體指數為102.6。

季度成長比單月結果穩健。第2季工業生產折合年率成長4%，製造業成長4.7%。修正值則略微下調近期表現：4月工業生產增幅由0.9%下修至0.8%，5月維持0.1%；5月製造業產出則由持平上修為增加0.1%。

產能利用率維持76.1%，較1972至2025年的平均低3.3個百分點。即使產出在本季增加，這項差距仍顯示工業部門存在閒置產能。對聯準會而言，數據既未發出經濟成長突然惡化的警訊，也未呈現足以單獨強化近期升息理由的廣泛製造業加速。

消費者信心初值對家庭需求釋出較正面的訊號。汽油價格下降改善消費者對自身財務及經濟的看法，使7月初信心升至5個月高點。未來一年通膨預期由6月的4.6%降至4.2%，減輕先前油價衝擊立即固化於家庭預期的疑慮；不過，這項調查進行時，尚未涵蓋週五原油新一波漲勢的大部分。

Hammack的談話使政策焦點維持在實際通膨及其廣度。這位今年擁有FOMC投票權的克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁表示，通膨仍然過高，勞動市場則接近她估計的充分就業。她認為兩項政策使命目前並無衝突，物價穩定因而是更迫切的目標。

她提出的證據不只來自官方通膨指標。Hammack表示，企業及社區領袖普遍反映能源成本、供應鏈中斷、保險費及AI熱潮帶來壓力。她就任克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁近兩年來，首次聽到部分企業表示央行必須採取行動抑制通膨；消費者則稱愈來愈難負擔生活成本。

Hammack並未預先承諾7月採取行動，並表示會以開放態度看待每次會議。不過，她的發言仍具重要性，因為這代表又有一名現任票委加入保留升息選項的陣營。達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan先前已明確主張升息，聯準會理事Christopher Waller及其他數名官員也曾警告，持續性通膨可能要求央行採取行動。

市場仍將這個較廣泛的政策陣營與下次會議區分看待。7月28至29日升息25個基點的隱含機率，由本週稍早約50%降至週五約15%。官員即將進入政策會議前的溝通緘默期，會前也沒有重大數據足以終結爭論，因此投資人認為7月升息可能性不高。

7月以後的緊縮預期則明顯穩固。聯準會主席Kevin Warsh強調，央行不能因單月通膨數據有利就宣告勝利，交易員仍反映年底前至少升息一次。週五2年期殖利率上升3.8個基點，是對這條後續路徑的部分調整，而不是推翻本週近期緊縮風險大幅降低的定價。

美債交易活動較先前通膨重新定價時清淡。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$7,590億，共286,226筆，較7月16日少16.2%。名目附息債交易量下降10.4%至$6,108億；不過，2年期以下名目附息債交易量增加27.6%至$1,531億。政策敏感殖利率上升之際，前端活動與整體周轉下降形成明顯差異。

7至10年期券種的面額交易量為$1,099億，下降17.6%；TIPS交易量下降19.2%至$168億。這些數字反映雙向成交，不能判定投資人方向，但進一步凸顯當日走勢的重心：最明顯的殖利率調整集中在政策期限附近，中長天期債券則變動不大或小幅上漲。

## 油價重建通膨風險，科技股回落

能源市場對6月通膨降溫論述構成最明確的挑戰。美國與伊朗軍隊連續第六天互相攻擊，航運業者轉趨謹慎，荷莫茲海峽通行量因而減少。戰事規模仍不及3月及4月初最激烈的階段，但商業航運受阻已足以使布蘭特原油週五盤中突破每桶$86，並推動兩項全球指標油價創4月以來最大單週漲幅。

WTI當日上漲4.48%至$82.49，週漲幅達15.52%；布蘭特原油上漲4.59%至$88.10，全週上漲15.91%。6月通膨報告反映的卻是汽油及能源價格下跌。這項時間差解釋了美債市場內部分歧：當前數據降低聯準會立即升息的理由，油價反彈則增加未來消費者及生產者物價逆轉部分改善的風險。

通膨並非唯一顧慮。荷莫茲海峽通行受限，可能同時推高能源送達成本並削弱經濟活動，進口依賴型經濟體尤其容易受影響。因此，即使通膨補償上升，成長風險仍可能支撐長天期政府債券。週五10年期實質殖利率下降、損益兩平通膨率上升，正與這兩股相反力量一致。

科技股賣壓也帶來另一股長天期債券需求。一項主要半導體指數創2025年4月以來最差單週表現，較歷史高點回落約20%。費城半導體指數全週下跌近10%，Nasdaq 100則跌4.13%。最新催化因素是Moonshot AI發布Kimi K3模型；這家中國公司表示，該模型足以與美國領先系統競爭。

市場擔憂不只是晶片需求是否會消失。價格較低但能力足夠的模型，可能增加整體運算資源用量，卻同時削弱個別模型開發商的定價能力。投資人更棘手的問題是：若美國的技術領先不再穩固，訓練及推論支出的最終回報更難證明，美國企業是否還會維持原有投資速度。

這項差異對固定收益市場相當重要，因為AI循環同時仰賴內部現金流與空前規模的債券發行。支出放緩可減少未來債券供給，卻也可能削弱支撐資料中心專案及科技借款人的收入假設；投資若持續，則會維持經濟需求與通膨壓力，同時要求信用投資人承擔更多產業曝險。週五股市下跌並未釐清最終由哪條路徑主導。

整體跨資產走勢偏向避險，但未陷入失序。S&P 500下跌1.01%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.49%，半導體指數跌1.63%。VIX升至18.77，但仍遠低於嚴重市場壓力時的水準。美元指數收於100.75，漲幅不到0.01%，顯示市場並未普遍搶進美元流動性。黃金重回$4,000以上，但對未來政策利率上升的預期抵銷地緣政治需求，使其全週仍然下跌。

週五固定收益市場截止時間後的事件進一步升高能源風險，但不能用來解釋已完成的美債收盤。週末期間，伊朗攻擊造成駐約旦及伊拉克美軍人員死亡，雙方也加速攻擊非純軍事目標。伊朗鎖定科威特一座電力及海水淡化設施，美軍則攻擊波斯灣及伊朗南部地點。亞洲早盤布蘭特原油升破每桶$91，使美債投資人在現貨交易恢復時必須面對更大的價格衝擊。

## AI借款考驗全球信貸市場承接深度

科技股回落之際，為AI基礎設施融資而發行的債券也逐步重新定價。隨著發行量增速超過許多以指數為基準的投資組合所能從容吸收的程度，超大規模雲端業者以美元、歐元、英鎊、日圓及瑞士法郎發行的債券普遍表現落後。

2025年初以來，該產業發行的債券約有79%交易利差比首日更寬，價格平均較發行價下跌3.3點，平均總報酬為負1.4%。這些借款人仍是全球信用市場中財務實力最強的企業之一，但其疲弱表現說明，信用素質本身無法使投資人免受供給、存續期間及集中度風險影響。

Alphabet、Meta、Amazon及Oracle自2025年初以來發債逾$3,000億，其中接近$800億以美元以外幣別計價。跨市場借款使企業得以分散資金來源，也大幅提高其在各地債券指數中的重要性。Alphabet已成為一項英鎊投資級指數中最大的非金融發行人，Amazon與Alphabet也躋身瑞士法郎市場四大借款人之列。

發債規模擴大後，被動式基金與受基準限制的經理人，不論是否願意主動配置科技業，曝險都隨之增加。每筆新交易都拉高科技業權重，迫使買方承擔更多彼此相關的風險，包括資料中心建設、晶片供應、電力需求，以及AI服務帶來的收入。

Amazon在7月稍早發行的$250億債券，使這項顧慮更為突出。該交易是AI相關大型發行中超額認購程度最低者之一，而且時點接近企業發債通常進入夏季淡季之初。因此，次級市場表現疲弱不只是某個特別繁忙交易日供給擁擠的結果，也顯示即使進入季節性較清淡時期，投資人仍可能持續要求發行讓利。

信用違約交換也呈現類似訊號。2025年以來活躍於債券市場的超大規模雲端業者，其違約保障成本擴大幅度高於北美整體指標。這不代表市場預期這些公司會違約，而是投資人要求更高補償，以承擔反覆借款及AI資本支出經濟回報不確定的組合風險。

保險公司是投資級公司債的重要需求來源，目前對該產業的配置仍遠低於正式集中度上限。較高的整體殖利率也使這些債券持續吸引長期投資人。因此，限制並非需求消失，而是每一波新增供給需要何種價格才能完成銷售。若供給到來的速度持續快於投資組合願意增加曝險的速度，即使企業實力強健，其債券相對評等仍可能顯得便宜。

壓力也延伸至大型上市科技集團以外。Prime Data Centers延後一筆原擬依挪威法律發行的債券，進一步顯示資料中心融資市場的篩選趨嚴。若借款人依賴較集中的客戶群或特定專案現金流，而非多元化企業資產負債表，風險尤其明顯。

擔保貸款憑證則面臨另一種侵蝕。規模$1.3兆的CLO市場仍按承諾向優先券層持有人付款，但最次順位股權層的報酬已大幅惡化。第1季CLO股權報酬為負15%，部分高度曝險的基金已削減股利，或警告股東未來情況可能更加困難。

惡化源自支撐CLO股權層的套利空間受到擠壓。投資工具賺取企業貸款擔保品報酬與支付給有評等債券持有人利息之間的差額；貸款表現疲弱、可取得的資產利差下降，加上市場對CLO債券需求持續，都使股權層可分配的剩餘現金減少。併購交易匱乏也限制了新承作貸款的供給，加劇對擔保品的競爭。

軟體業貸款走弱，進一步加重既有投資組合損失。同時，由CLO經理人控制的自有股權基金，使交易更容易在沒有獨立第三方買方審視最高風險券層的情況下推出。這種架構能在市場受挫時維持發行運作，但也令人質疑，在投資工具成立前，經濟條件較弱的交易是否受到足夠約束。

壓力已在XFLT明顯浮現。這檔規模$5.8億、持有大量CLO股權的上市基金，兩年內價值下跌50%。董事會以淨資產價值表現疲弱為由，尋求由King Street旗下Rockford Tower取代Octagon Credit Investors。Octagon則反駁其表現優於可比CLO基金，並要求撤換董事會。股東預定於7月30日表決更換經理人。

這項爭議並不表示優先順位CLO債券普遍受損，但確實顯示原本用來吸收波動的結構部位，損失已大到足以迫使業者調整管理團隊、股利及資產配置。長期與CLO股權投資密切相關的Eagle Point正轉向基礎設施貸款及設備融資，並表示市場可能連續第二年錄得年度虧損。

整體信用基金價格週五僅小幅波動。LQD上漲0.06%，HYG下跌0.19%，JNK下跌0.10%，EMB下跌0.06%。真正具影響力的重新定價仍集中於特定結構及融資主題，包括超大規模雲端業者供給、資料中心曝險及CLO股權次順位部位的經濟性，而非資金全面撤離公司債或新興市場債。

## 槓桿借款人讓利後才完成融資

Cotality完成今年美國規模最大的槓桿融資再籌資交易之一，化解前一日難以吸引需求的困境。這家房地產資料公司把部分融資由債券轉為貸款、提高投資人報酬，並加強防範庭外重整操作的債權人保障後，籌得$52.5億。

最終融資方案包括一筆$28億定期貸款，利率比基準高4.25個百分點，發行價為每美元98美分。Cotality另按面額發行$16.5億第一順位垃圾債，殖利率為9%。風險最高的$8億第二順位債券，則以每美元95美分定價，殖利率約13.3%，為2026年美國發行的垃圾債中最高。

這些條件明顯高於公司最初預期的融資成本。交易證明大型再融資仍可進入市場，但借款人必須調整資金組合、提供更多契約保障，並接受可觀的整體成本。Cotality將用募集資金償還原先為Stone Point Capital與Insight Partners以$60億收購該公司而籌措的債務。

公司的資產負債表幾乎沒有餘裕承受不佳的發行條件。債務約為獲利的8倍，S&P給予的評等比投資級低6個級距。截至3月31日，Cotality持有約$5,500萬現金。Moody’s預期，在未來一年自由現金流仍極有限的情況下，公司將依靠循環信用額度支應營運；S&P則預期再融資後債務服務成本將上升。

Foundever與債權人達成更全面的協議，以降低債務並為公司進行資本重整。參與貸款人將把每美元既有債權中的57.5美分換成新定期貸款，取得重整後公司約35%的股權，並共同分配$2.5億現金償債款。新證券也將提供更強的保障，防範未來的負債管理交易。

具控制權的Mulliez家族將投入$2.25億新股權，支應大部分現金付款，Foundever則由資產負債表出資$2,500萬。債權人指導委員會成員，包括Polus Capital Management與Sound Point Capital Management，預計可就所持貸款每美元額外獲得10美分回收款。

交易預計使Foundever減債約$9億，並包含管理階層異動。執行長Laurent Uberti預定離任，由Mulliez家族成員Benoit Leclercq暫代。這次重整是在歷經數月協商後達成；公司資產負債表因2021年以$22億收購Sykes Enterprises而承受壓力，商業模式也面臨客戶自行開發AI服務工具的競爭。

Baker Tilly則準備朝相反方向移動，由私人信貸轉進廣泛聯貸市場。德意志銀行計畫安排投資人會議，為可能約$30億的交易探詢需求，以再融資這家會計師事務所擴張及與Moss Adams合併所使用的貸款。Blackstone先前主導約$15億私人融資，為合併提供利率比基準高4.5個百分點的資金。

這項擬議再融資將檢驗，在經歷併購帶動的成長後，公開槓桿貸款及債券投資人是否願意取代私人貸款機構。自Hellman & Friedman於2024年收購Baker Tilly以來，公司持續併購地區型會計師事務所。債務移往公開市場可以擴大資金來源，但在Cotality大幅讓利後，最終能否完成仍取決於槓桿、文件條款及投資人要求的價格。

其他借款人則在測試特定資金池的需求。阿根廷內烏肯省準備於7月20日在紐約展開路演，發行最多$5億國際債券，這將是該省自2017年以來首次新發外債。官員希望採用5至7年期到期一次償還結構，利率介於7%至8%。該省受惠於頁岩油產量增加，並預期整個地區到本十年末日產量將接近100萬桶。

繼科爾多瓦省、丘布特省及布宜諾斯艾利斯市近期發行國際債券後，這筆交易顯示阿根廷地方政府正在利用利差收窄的機會，即使中央政府仍避免重返全球市場。內烏肯省的石油收入提供特定信用支撐，但到期一次償還結構會使再融資風險集中於到期日。

巴西則準備以另一種方式進入主權債市場。政府計畫透過首次在中國境內發行熊貓債，籌集約人民幣100億元、相當於$14.8億，時間可能在年底前。這將是拉丁美洲主權發行人首筆熊貓債，目的在為擁有中國收入或業務的巴西企業建立定價基準。

2026年至今熊貓債發行量已創人民幣1,730億元紀錄，較2025年同期增加約70%；外國企業借款人的平均票息則降至1.97%。低票息未必等於低整體成本，因為借款人可能需要把募集資金換成美元或其他營運貨幣。迄今唯一進入該市場的拉丁美洲企業發行人Suzano表示，經換匯後的融資成本仍低於可比美元債。

這項融資管道可能仍具選擇性。首次申請核准可耗時5至6個月，一般交易規模較小、期限較短，中國投資人也偏好評等較高的發行人。對中國出口比重較高的企業，比起只想尋找美元市場一般替代管道的較低評等借款人，更能直接運用人民幣資金或有效避險。

聖安東尼奧也將測試大型市政融資需求。該市計畫於7月21日為約$9.44億機場債定價，到期年分橫跨2027至2060年。募集資金將支援一項為期20年的擴建計畫，核心工程是造價約$17億、最多可設18個登機門的新航廈。機場預期2040年旅客量將接近1,500萬人次。

這批債券獲Moody’s與S&P分別給予A2及A+評等。美國機場債發行量在2025年創$240億紀錄後，2026年上半年較一年前下降約24%，本次發行將檢驗長天期市政債需求。交易進行之際，美債長端殖利率仍高，企業借款人也在爭奪投資人承接長天期部位的能力。

## 歐洲通膨降溫，亞洲央行保留政策彈性

歐元區通膨終值確認6月明顯減速，時點在歐洲央行7月23日會議之前。HICP年增率由5月的3.2%降至2.8%，符合初值；物價月減0.1%。歐盟成員國中有22國通膨放緩、3國持平，僅2國上升，顯示降溫範圍遍及多數地區。

服務仍是年增率最大貢獻來源，貢獻1.51個百分點；能源貢獻0.77個百分點，食品、酒類及菸草貢獻0.29個百分點，非能源工業產品則貢獻0.18個百分點。分項顯示通膨問題已不再全面加劇，但服務與能源仍占超出目標部分的大多數。一年前歐元區通膨率為2%。

經濟學家一致預期ECB將在本次會議維持存款利率不變。多數人預測9月將再升息25個基點至2.5%，屆時決策官員會取得最新工作人員預測。市場預期暫停，是因6月通膨改善、薪資帶動第二輪效應的證據有限，而不是確信能源風險已經消失。

9月是否升息，仍取決於荷莫茲海峽受阻持續多久。若衝擊受控，ECB在6月升息後停止緊縮的空間會更大；若油氣運輸長期中斷，則可能推高通膨預期及營運成本。受訪經濟學家僅9%認為已有通膨預期失去錨定的證據，多數人也不特別擔心第二輪效應；不過，戰事再起仍使ECB難以排除緊縮選項。

9月前公布的經濟活動數據，將決定再次升息是否適度。6月綜合採購經理人指數正好為50，位於擴張與萎縮的分界。9月決策前還將公布兩次通膨數據、第2季經濟成長及更多企業調查。ECB因此有時間區分進口能源衝擊與較廣泛的通膨過程，也能觀察已經收緊的信貸條件是否削弱需求。

日本的政策討論朝不同方向發展。日本央行官員正考慮上調截至明年3月止財政年度的成長預測，目前預測為0.5%；7月會議則料維持政策利率不變。央行6月已把利率升至1%，創1995年以來最高，再度立即升息的可能性不高。

可能上修預測，是因全球AI需求更強，企業也在中東衝突期間成功找到替代原料來源。科技相關產品出口價格上升，部分抵銷進口能源變貴對日本貿易條件的損害。官員也在考慮淡化目前「成長風險偏向下行」的評估。

通膨仍不支持央行宣告正常化已經完成。企業把較高成本轉嫁給消費者的速度快於以往；日本央行預期，其偏好的通膨指標在此前連續4個財政年度高於目標後，未來兩個財政年度仍將維持2%以上。隔夜交換市場顯示10月前再升息的機率約為69%。6月升息後接受調查的經濟學家中，約半數預期12月升息，36%選擇10月。

日圓接近1986年以來最弱水準，提高了等待的代價，但政府立場仍是不確定因素。首相高市早苗傾向維持寬鬆貨幣政策。修訂版政府經濟政策方針納入尊重日本央行獨立性的文字，投資人仍將檢視最終文件是否試圖影響緊縮速度。

日本3個月期國庫券標售提供了最新短端融資結果。財務省按加權平均價格99.7634接受競標，金額為¥2.898兆，相當於0.9618%殖利率。最低得標價格為99.7615，相當於0.9695%，該價格的配售比例為30.3121%。國庫券於7月21日發行、10月19日到期，競爭性投標總額達¥11.572兆。需求相當充足，但未解決下一次日本央行升息時點的政策爭論。

印度更直接暴露於食品及能源供給風險。印度央行總裁Sanjay Malhotra表示，通膨近18個月來首次超過央行4%目標後，仍處於高檔。他認為大部分壓力來自供給因素，但指出中東衝突及雨季降雨不足是前景面臨的主要威脅。

印度近90%的石油依賴進口，其中接近一半通常經荷莫茲海峽運送。因此，原油再度上漲提高成本向國內更廣泛傳導的風險。降雨量比長期平均少23%，威脅農作物播種；印度全年約70%的降水來自雨季。前農業部次長Siraj Hussain表示，食品通膨可能超過7%，豆類與油籽尤其取決於截至8月底的降雨分布。

RBI在2026年全年均把政策利率維持於5.25%，並表示若物價壓力擴散將採取行動。Malhotra仍認為此時緊縮為時過早，主張等待更多證據。央行也把經濟成長預測由6.9%下調至6.6%，顯示在通膨尚未廣泛到足以觸發升息之前，石油衝擊已會讓進口依賴型經濟體付出成長代價。RBI下次會議定於8月3至5日。

## 前瞻市場意涵

ECB於7月23日的決策是第一項重大政策考驗。市場普遍預期利率不變，焦點將落在總裁Christine Lagarde如何描述9月政策。6月通膨降至2.8%，服務價格壓力緩和，第二輪效應的證據仍有限；不過，若荷莫茲海峽持續受阻，再升息的理由仍在。反之，經濟活動轉弱及能源價格穩定，將降低進一步緊縮的必要性。

同日美國財政部將於美東時間13:00標售$210億新發10年期抗通膨債券，7月31日交割，2036年7月15日到期。週五10年期實質殖利率下降1.9個基點、損益兩平通膨率上升1.4個基點後，本次標售將檢驗市場對實質長天期部位及明確通膨保障的需求。油價收盤後進一步上漲，也使兩項殖利率組成的差異格外重要。

日本6月全國消費者物價指數將於7月24日公布。數據將協助判斷，日本央行較樂觀的成長評估及企業加快成本轉嫁，是否足以支持最快10月再升息，或讓官員等到12月。投資人在1%政策利率與通膨持續高於目標之間權衡時，結果也會影響日圓及國內JGB需求。

英國6月零售銷售將於7月24日英國夏令時間07:00公布。英國正承受進口能源成本上升及政治領導層變動，家庭需求將是英國央行政策的重要限制。消費若具韌性，央行將有更多空間回應通膨；需求若疲弱，則會凸顯進一步緊縮的成長代價。

美國6月新屋銷售將於7月24日美東時間10:00公布，為週五住宅建設報告提供需求面的對照。住宅開工大增19%主要由多戶住宅推動，獨棟住宅開工及建築許可均下降。銷售數據將顯示完工庫存能否找到買家，或房貸成本是否仍壓抑住宅市場中對美債殖利率最敏感的部分。

7月28至29日FOMC會議仍是美國最重要的政策事件。市場已把立即升息的機率降至約15%，官員進入溝通緘默期後，重塑這項預期的能力有限。更重要的問題是，在非燃料進口物價上升、Hammack強調企業廣泛擔憂通膨，以及油價抹去部分6月能源成本舒緩後，Warsh將如何描述後續政策路徑。

信用交易也會提供另一項市場考驗。聖安東尼奧$9.44億機場債定於7月21日定價，Baker Tilly擬議的$30億再融資則進入投資人會議；內烏肯省同日開始推銷預計發行的$5億國際債券。結果將顯示投資人對長天期市政債、併購支撐的槓桿債務，以及能源收入支撐的新興市場信用，仍會做出多大程度的差異化配置。

固定收益市場的關鍵問題，已不再是單週有利的通膨數據是否排除聯準會7月升息；殖利率曲線與政策定價已反映這項結論。尚未解決的考驗是，在美國需求仍具韌性、AI投資持續支撐經濟活動、成本及借款之際，6月通膨降溫能否抵禦新一波油價衝擊。週五趨平的美債殖利率曲線捕捉到這項不確定性：經濟成長不均及科技股下跌支撐長端，但前端仍無法排除只是延後、而非確定結束的升息循環。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries finished July 17 with a sharp distinction between immediate Federal Reserve risk and longer-duration demand. The 2-year yield rose 3.8 basis points to 4.18%, while the 5-year added 0.9 basis point to 4.279%. The 10-year yield slipped 0.5 basis point to 4.549%, and the 30-year fell 1.3 basis points to 5.071%. That produced a bearish flattening at the front of the curve: 2s10s narrowed 4.3 basis points to 36.9 basis points and 2s30s compressed 5.1 basis points to 89.1 basis points.

The session did not overturn the week’s inflation-driven Treasury advance. The 2-year yield remained 2.9 basis points lower than a week earlier and the 10-year was down 1.3 basis points. It did, however, show why traders were reluctant to extend the rally indiscriminately. June import prices recorded another increase, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said persistent inflation was her principal concern, and WTI and Brent crude surged roughly 4.5% as renewed U.S.-Iran attacks further disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Those developments kept the prospect of tightening later in the year alive even as traders largely abandoned the possibility of a July increase.

The day’s economic releases were mixed beneath their headlines. Housing starts jumped 19% to a 1.427 million annual rate, but the increase was concentrated in multifamily construction while single-family starts edged lower and permits declined. Industrial production rose only 0.1%, manufacturing output was unchanged and capacity utilization remained well below its long-run average. Import prices increased 0.3% and were 7.1% higher than a year earlier, the fastest annual gain since August 2022, even though the monthly energy contribution receded.

That combination helped explain why the long end could recover while the front end sold off. The 10-year real yield fell 1.9 basis points to 2.295%, consistent with the uneven activity detail and demand for duration during a technology-led equity decline. The 10-year breakeven inflation rate rose 1.4 basis points to 2.254%, reflecting the renewed energy shock and the persistence of nonfuel import costs. The small decline in the nominal 10-year yield was therefore the net result of lower real rates and higher inflation compensation rather than a uniform disinflation move.

Oil and technology supplied opposing pressures on broader risk assets. WTI settled at $82.49 and Brent at $88.10, leaving both almost 16% higher over the week. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.49%, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 1.63% and the S&P 500 declined 1.01% as investors questioned the economics of the artificial-intelligence investment cycle after a new Chinese model intensified competition. The VIX rose 12.19% to 18.77. Gold gained 0.68% to $4,012.70, though it remained 2.23% lower for the week, while the dollar index was nearly unchanged.

The same AI reassessment was increasingly visible in corporate bonds. More than $300 billion of borrowing by four large technology companies since the beginning of 2025 has made their debt a significant part of global credit indexes, and much of it has underperformed since issuance. That supply pressure remained distinct from immediate default risk: the borrowers are financially strong, but repeated large transactions require investors to absorb growing issuer and sector concentrations. In leveraged finance, Cotality completed its difficult $5.25 billion refinancing only after increasing yields, shifting more funding into loans and strengthening creditor protections. The contrast showed that credit remained available, but its terms were becoming more sensitive to leverage, documentation and the durability of the investment story behind each borrower.

## Mixed U.S. Data Leave the Fed’s Later Path Open

June trade prices added a less benign inflation signal after the week’s softer consumer- and producer-price reports. Import prices rose 0.3% from May, following an upwardly revised 1.7% increase, and were 7.1% higher than a year earlier. The annual advance was the largest since August 2022. Export prices fell 0.6% on the month after a revised 1.2% May increase, but their 12-month gain remained 10.2%.

The import-price composition separated current energy relief from broader cost pressure. Fuel import prices fell 0.4% after surging 12.6% in May. Petroleum prices declined 0.7%, while imported natural-gas prices rose 9.2%. Nonfuel import prices increased 0.4% in June and 4.2% over the year, leaving a pipeline of traded-goods inflation that could persist even without another monthly fuel increase. Agricultural export prices rose 0.2%, while prices for nonagricultural exports fell 0.7%.

The figures did not negate June’s favorable CPI and PPI results, which had already driven a large reduction in expectations for a July rate increase. They did make the inflation improvement less uniform. Consumer and producer energy prices had benefited from June’s decline in gasoline and crude, while import prices showed continuing pressure outside fuels. The subsequent rebound in oil means the favorable monthly fuel comparison is unlikely to describe the active July cost environment.

Housing presented a similarly divided picture. Total starts rose 19% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.427 million from a revised 1.199 million in May. Construction of buildings with at least 5 units reached a 513,000 rate, accounting for most of the headline acceleration. Single-family starts slipped 0.2% to 895,000, offering little evidence that lower June inflation had yet relieved the affordability and financing constraints reported by homebuilders.

The forward-looking measures were softer. Building permits fell 3% to a 1.367 million annual rate, including a 2.4% decline in single-family permits to 871,000. Completions rose 3.3% overall to 1.392 million, and single-family completions increased 6.6% to 964,000. The data therefore showed a burst of current construction and a larger flow of finished homes, but not a broad strengthening in plans for future residential building.

Industrial production continued to expand without reproducing the strength in several regional factory surveys. Total output rose 0.1% in June and was 1.1% higher than a year earlier. Manufacturing output was unchanged, while mining and utilities each increased 0.4%. The aggregate index stood at 102.6.

Quarterly growth was firmer than the monthly result. Industrial production advanced at a 4% annual rate in Q2, and manufacturing rose at a 4.7% rate. Revisions also softened the recent history slightly: April production was marked down to 0.8% from 0.9%, while May remained at 0.1%. May manufacturing was revised to a 0.1% increase from no change.

Capacity utilization held at 76.1%, 3.3 percentage points below its 1972–2025 average. That gap indicated continuing industrial slack even as output increased over the quarter. For the Fed, the release supplied neither an abrupt growth warning nor the broad manufacturing acceleration that would independently strengthen the case for near-term tightening.

Preliminary consumer-sentiment figures were more encouraging about household demand. Sentiment rose to a 5-month high in early July as lower gasoline prices improved consumers’ assessments of their finances and the economy. Expected inflation over the following year declined to 4.2% from 4.6% in June. The decrease eased concern that the earlier oil shock was immediately becoming embedded in household expectations, although the survey preceded much of Friday’s renewed rise in crude.

Hammack’s remarks kept the policy emphasis on realized inflation and its breadth. The Cleveland Fed president, who votes on the Federal Open Market Committee this year, said inflation remained too high while the labor market was near her estimate of maximum employment. That balance left no conflict between the Fed’s mandates in her assessment and made price stability the more urgent objective.

Her evidence extended beyond official inflation measures. Hammack said businesses and community leaders were reporting widespread pressure from energy costs, supply-chain disruption, insurance premiums and the AI boom. For the first time since she became Cleveland Fed president almost 2 years earlier, some businesses were telling her that the central bank needed to act to curb inflation. Consumers, meanwhile, were describing greater difficulty meeting living costs.

Hammack did not pre-commit to a July move and said she would approach each meeting with an open mind. Her intervention nevertheless mattered because it added a current, voting official to the group preserving the option of higher rates. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan had already explicitly called for an increase, while Governor Christopher Waller and several other policymakers had warned that persistent inflation could require action.

The market continued to separate that broader coalition from the next meeting. The implied probability of a quarter-point increase on July 28–29 fell to about 15% by Friday from roughly 50% earlier in the week. With officials entering their communications blackout and no major release expected to settle the debate before the meeting, investors treated a July move as unlikely.

Expectations beyond July remained much firmer. Traders continued to price at least one increase by year-end as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh emphasized that the central bank could not declare victory after one favorable inflation month. The 2-year yield’s 3.8-basis-point rise on Friday represented a partial adjustment toward that later path, not a reversal of the week’s large reduction in immediate tightening risk.

Treasury activity was lighter than during the preceding inflation repricing. FINRA recorded $759 billion of par trading across 286,226 transactions, 16.2% less activity than on July 16. Nominal-coupon volume fell 10.4% to $610.8 billion. Trading in nominal coupons of 2 years or less increased 27.6% to $153.1 billion, however, distinguishing the front end from the broader decline in turnover as policy-sensitive yields rose.

The 7- to 10-year sector recorded $109.9 billion of par activity, down 17.6%, while TIPS activity fell 19.2% to $16.8 billion. Those figures describe two-way turnover rather than investor direction, but they reinforce the session’s concentration: the most visible yield adjustment occurred near the policy horizon, while intermediate and long maturities changed little or rallied modestly.

## Oil Rebuilds Inflation Risk as Technology Shares Retreat

Energy markets supplied the clearest challenge to the June disinflation narrative. U.S. and Iranian forces traded attacks for a sixth consecutive day, while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz declined as shippers became more cautious. The fighting remained less extensive than during the heaviest phase of the war in March and early April, but the disruption to commercial shipping was sufficient to push Brent above $86 during Friday trading and leave both global benchmarks with their largest weekly advances since April.

WTI’s 4.48% daily gain to $82.49 brought its weekly increase to 15.52%. Brent rose 4.59% to $88.10 and gained 15.91% over the week. Those moves occurred after June inflation reports had captured falling gasoline and energy prices. The timing explains the divergence inside the Treasury market: current data reduced the case for an immediate Fed increase, while the oil rebound lifted the risk that later consumer and producer prices will reverse part of that improvement.

The inflation effect was not the only concern. Restricted Hormuz traffic threatened an adverse combination of higher delivered energy costs and weaker activity, particularly in import-dependent economies. That left long-duration government bonds with a potential growth offset even as inflation compensation rose. Friday’s decline in the 10-year real yield and increase in the breakeven rate were consistent with those competing forces.

The technology selloff created another source of duration demand. A key semiconductor gauge completed its worst week since April 2025 and fell about 20% from its record. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost nearly 10% during the week, while the Nasdaq 100 declined 4.13%. The latest catalyst was Moonshot AI’s release of its Kimi K3 model, which the Chinese company said could compete with leading U.S. systems.

The market concern extended beyond whether chip demand would disappear. Cheaper, capable models can increase total use of computing resources while reducing the pricing power of individual model developers. The more difficult question for investors was whether U.S. companies would continue investing at the same pace if technological leadership proved less durable and the eventual returns on training and inference spending became harder to defend.

That distinction mattered for fixed income because the AI cycle is being financed through both internal cash flow and unprecedented bond issuance. Slower spending would reduce prospective debt supply but could also weaken the revenue assumptions supporting data-center projects and technology borrowers. Continued spending would preserve economic demand and inflation pressure while asking credit investors to absorb still more sector exposure. Friday’s equity decline did not resolve which path would dominate.

The broader cross-asset move was risk-averse without becoming disorderly. The S&P 500 fell 1.01%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.49% and the semiconductor index declined 1.63%. The VIX rose to 18.77 but remained well below levels associated with severe market stress. The dollar index ended at 100.75, up less than 0.01%, showing little generalized scramble for dollar liquidity. Gold recovered above $4,000 but still posted a weekly loss as higher prospective policy rates competed with geopolitical demand.

Events after Friday’s fixed-income cutoff increased the energy risk without explaining the completed Treasury close. Over the weekend, Iranian attacks killed U.S. service members in Jordan and Iraq, and the two sides accelerated strikes beyond purely military targets. Iran targeted a power and desalination facility in Kuwait, while U.S. forces attacked locations in the Persian Gulf and southern Iran. In early Asian trading, Brent rose above $91 a barrel, extending the price shock that Treasury investors will confront when cash trading resumes.

## AI Borrowing Tests the Depth of Global Credit

The retreat in technology shares coincided with a more gradual repricing of the bonds issued to fund AI infrastructure. Debt sold by hyperscalers has underperformed across dollars, euros, sterling, yen and Swiss francs as the volume of issuance increased faster than many benchmarked portfolios could comfortably absorb.

About 79% of the sector’s bonds issued since early 2025 were trading at wider spreads than on their first day, and the securities had fallen an average of 3.3 points from issue price. Their average total return was negative 1.4%. The borrowers remained among the strongest companies in global credit, but the weak performance showed that credit quality alone did not protect investors from supply, duration and concentration risk.

Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Oracle issued more than $300 billion of debt from the beginning of 2025. Close to $80 billion was denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar. That cross-market borrowing allowed the companies to diversify their funding base, but it also transformed their importance in local bond indexes. Alphabet became the largest nonfinancial issuer in a sterling high-grade index, while Amazon and Alphabet ranked among the four largest borrowers in the Swiss-franc market.

The expansion left passive funds and benchmark-constrained managers with increasing exposure whether or not they wanted to make an active sector allocation. Each new transaction enlarged technology weights and required buyers to accept more correlated risk tied to data-center construction, chip availability, power demand and the revenue produced by AI services.

Amazon’s $25 billion transaction earlier in July sharpened the concern. It recorded some of the lowest oversubscription levels for a jumbo AI-related offering and arrived near the beginning of the usual summer slowdown in corporate issuance. The weak aftermarket was therefore not simply the result of crowded supply on one especially busy day; it raised the prospect that investors would require sustained concessions even during a seasonally quieter period.

Credit-default swaps told a similar story. Protection costs for hyperscalers active in the bond market since 2025 widened more than the broader North American benchmark. That did not imply an expectation of default. It showed that investors were demanding more compensation for the combination of repeated borrowing and uncertainty about the economic return on AI capital expenditure.

Insurers, an important source of demand for high-grade corporate bonds, remained well below formal concentration limits for the sector. Elevated all-in yields also continued to make the bonds attractive to long-horizon buyers. The constraint was therefore not the disappearance of demand but the price required to clear each additional wave of issuance. Strong companies can remain cheap to their ratings if supply keeps arriving faster than portfolios want to increase exposure.

The pressure extended beyond large public technology groups. Prime Data Centers postponed a planned bond under Norwegian law, adding to the evidence that data-center financing was becoming more selective. The risk was especially pronounced where the borrower depended on a narrower customer base or a specific project’s cash flows rather than a diversified corporate balance sheet.

Collateralized-loan obligations faced a different form of erosion. The $1.3 trillion CLO market continued to pay holders of senior tranches as promised, but returns on the most subordinated equity pieces had deteriorated sharply. CLO equity returned negative 15% in Q1, and some funds with large exposure reduced dividends or warned shareholders of further difficulty.

The deterioration reflected pressure on the arbitrage that supports CLO equity. Vehicles earn the difference between returns on corporate-loan collateral and the interest paid to rated bondholders. Weak loan performance, lower available asset spreads and continuing demand for CLO debt reduced the residual cash left for the equity layer. A dearth of mergers also limited the supply of newly originated loans, increasing competition for collateral.

Software-loan weakness added losses to existing portfolios. At the same time, captive-equity funds controlled by CLO managers made it easier to launch deals without independent third-party buyers scrutinizing the riskiest tranche. That structure can keep issuance functioning during market setbacks, but it also raises questions about whether weaker economics receive enough discipline before a vehicle is created.

The strain became visible at XFLT, a $580 million listed fund with substantial CLO-equity exposure whose value declined 50% over 2 years. Its board sought to replace Octagon Credit Investors with a King Street affiliate, Rockford Tower, blaming weak net-asset-value performance. Octagon countered that it had outperformed comparable CLO funds and called for the board to be replaced. Shareholders are scheduled to vote on the manager change on July 30.

The dispute does not show broad impairment of senior CLO debt. It does demonstrate that the part of the structure designed to absorb volatility is producing losses large enough to force changes in management, dividends and asset allocation. Eagle Point, long associated with CLO equity, has been shifting toward infrastructure loans and equipment financing and said the market may record a second consecutive annual loss.

Broad credit-fund prices moved only modestly on Friday. LQD gained 0.06%, while HYG fell 0.19%, JNK declined 0.10% and EMB lost 0.06%. The consequential repricing remained concentrated in particular structures and funding themes: hyperscaler supply, data-center exposure and the subordinated economics of CLO equity rather than a uniform withdrawal from corporate or emerging-market debt.

## Leveraged Borrowers Clear Only After Concessions

Cotality completed one of the year’s largest U.S. leveraged-finance refinancings, resolving the transaction that had struggled to attract demand a day earlier. The property-data company raised $5.25 billion after shifting part of the financing from bonds into loans, increasing investor returns and strengthening protections against out-of-court restructuring maneuvers.

The final package included a $2.8 billion term loan priced 4.25 percentage points over its benchmark and issued at 98 cents on the dollar. Cotality also sold $1.65 billion of first-lien junk bonds at par to yield 9%. The riskiest piece, an $800 million second-lien bond, priced at 95 cents to yield about 13.3%, the highest yield on any U.S. junk bond issued in 2026.

Those terms were materially more expensive than the company had initially contemplated. They established that the market remained open for a large refinancing, but only after the borrower changed the funding mix, provided additional covenant protection and accepted a substantial all-in cost. Cotality will use the proceeds to repay debt originally raised to finance its $6 billion acquisition by Stone Point Capital and Insight Partners.

The company’s balance sheet left little room for a weak execution. Debt was equivalent to roughly 8 times earnings, and S&P rated the borrower 6 notches below investment grade. Cotality held about $55 million of cash on March 31. Moody’s expected it to rely on a revolving facility to fund operations as free cash flow remained very modest over the following year, while S&P anticipated higher debt-service costs after the refinancing.

Foundever reached a more comprehensive agreement with creditors to reduce debt and recapitalize the business. Participating lenders will exchange 57.5 cents of each dollar of existing claims for a new term loan, receive roughly 35% of the equity in the restructured company and share a $250 million cash paydown. The securities will carry stronger protection against future liability-management transactions.

The controlling Mulliez family will provide $225 million of new equity to finance most of the cash payment, while Foundever will contribute $25 million from its balance sheet. Members of the creditor steering committee, including Polus Capital Management and Sound Point Capital Management, are due to receive an additional 10 cents on the dollar of recovery on their loans.

The transaction is expected to reduce Foundever’s debt by about $900 million. It also includes a management change: Chief Executive Officer Laurent Uberti is set to depart, with Mulliez family member Benoit Leclercq taking over on an interim basis. The restructuring follows months of talks over a balance sheet burdened by the $2.2 billion acquisition of Sykes Enterprises in 2021 and a business model facing competition from customers developing AI-based service tools internally.

Baker Tilly was preparing to move in the opposite direction, from private credit into broadly syndicated debt markets. Deutsche Bank planned investor meetings for a potential transaction of about $3 billion to refinance loans used for the accounting firm’s expansion and its merger with Moss Adams. Blackstone had led roughly $1.5 billion of private financing at 4.5 percentage points over the benchmark for the merger.

The proposed refinancing would show whether public leveraged-loan and bond investors are willing to replace private lenders after a period of acquisition-led growth. Baker Tilly has continued buying regional accounting firms since Hellman & Friedman acquired it in 2024. Moving the debt could broaden the funding base, but final execution will depend on leverage, documentation and the price required by investors after Cotality’s large concessions.

Other borrowers were testing specialized pools of demand. Argentina’s Neuquén province prepared to begin a New York roadshow on July 20 for as much as $500 million of international bonds, its first new external issue since 2017. Officials were seeking a 5- to 7-year bullet maturity with an interest rate between 7% and 8%. The province is benefiting from higher shale production and expects output from the wider region to approach 1 million barrels a day by the end of the decade.

The transaction would follow recent international issuance by Córdoba, Chubut and the city of Buenos Aires as Argentine sub-sovereigns take advantage of narrower spreads even while the national government avoids returning to global markets. Neuquén’s oil revenue offers a specific credit support, but a bullet structure would concentrate refinancing risk at maturity.

Brazil was preparing a different form of sovereign market access. The government aimed to raise about 10 billion yuan, or $1.48 billion, through its first onshore Chinese panda bond, potentially before the end of the year. The transaction would be the first by a Latin American sovereign and is intended to establish a benchmark for Brazilian companies with Chinese revenue or operations.

Panda issuance reached a record 173 billion yuan so far in 2026, about 70% more than in the comparable period of 2025, while average coupons for foreign corporate borrowers fell to 1.97%. The low coupon does not necessarily equal a low all-in cost because borrowers may need to swap proceeds into dollars or another operating currency. Suzano, the only Latin American corporate issuer in the market so far, said its swapped funding cost was still below that of comparable U.S. dollar debt.

The channel is likely to remain selective. First-time approvals can take 5 to 6 months, typical deals are relatively small and short, and Chinese investors favor higher-rated names. Companies with substantial exports to China are better placed to use yuan proceeds or hedge them efficiently than lower-rated borrowers seeking a general alternative to dollar markets.

San Antonio added a large municipal financing test. The city planned to price about $944 million of airport debt on July 21, with maturities from 2027 to 2060. Proceeds will support a 20-year expansion program centered on a new terminal costing roughly $1.7 billion and designed for as many as 18 gates. The airport expects passenger traffic to approach 15 million by 2040.

The bonds carry A2 and A+ ratings from Moody’s and S&P. Their execution will test long-duration municipal demand after U.S. airport issuance reached a record $24 billion in 2025 but fell about 24% year over year during the first half of 2026. The sale arrives while Treasury long yields remain elevated and corporate borrowers are also competing for investors’ duration capacity.

## Europe Disinflates as Asian Central Banks Retain Optionality

Final euro-area inflation confirmed a meaningful June deceleration before the European Central Bank’s July 23 meeting. Annual HICP inflation fell to 2.8% from 3.2% in May, matching the preliminary estimate, while prices declined 0.1% on the month. Inflation slowed in 22 European Union member states, was unchanged in 3 and increased in only 2, giving the moderation broad geographic reach.

Services remained the largest contributor, adding 1.51 percentage points to the annual rate. Energy contributed 0.77 point, food, alcohol and tobacco 0.29 point, and non-energy industrial goods 0.18 point. The component map showed that the inflation problem was no longer intensifying broadly, but services and energy still accounted for most of the overshoot. Euro-area inflation had been 2% a year earlier.

Economists unanimously expected the ECB to leave its deposit rate unchanged at the coming meeting. Most anticipated one additional 25-basis-point increase to 2.5% in September, when policymakers will receive updated staff forecasts. The expected pause reflected June’s inflation improvement and limited evidence of wage-driven second-round effects rather than confidence that the energy risk had disappeared.

The September call remained conditional on the duration of the Hormuz disruption. A contained episode would give the ECB greater scope to stop after June’s increase, while a prolonged interruption to oil and gas flows could lift expectations and operating costs. Only 9% of economists surveyed said there was evidence that inflation expectations were becoming unanchored, and most were not deeply concerned about second-round effects. Renewed fighting nevertheless made it difficult to close the tightening option.

Activity data arriving before September will determine whether another increase is proportionate. The June composite purchasing managers’ index was exactly 50, the dividing line between expansion and contraction. Two more inflation releases, Q2 growth and further business surveys will arrive before the September decision. That sequence gives the ECB time to distinguish an imported energy shock from a broader inflation process while observing whether already tighter credit conditions weaken demand.

Japan’s policy debate moved in a different direction. Bank of Japan officials were considering raising their growth projection from 0.5% for the fiscal year ending next March while leaving the policy rate unchanged at the July meeting. The bank had increased the rate to 1% in June, its highest since 1995, making another immediate move unlikely.

The prospective forecast revision reflected stronger global AI demand and companies’ success in finding alternative raw-material supplies despite the Middle East conflict. Higher export prices for technology-related products helped offset the deterioration in Japan’s terms of trade caused by more expensive imported energy. Officials were also considering softening their assessment that risks to growth were skewed to the downside.

Inflation continued to argue against declaring the normalization process complete. Businesses were passing higher costs to consumers more quickly than in the past, and the BOJ expected its preferred inflation measure to remain above 2% for the next 2 fiscal years after already exceeding the target during the previous 4. Overnight swaps assigned about a 69% probability to another increase by October, while roughly half the economists surveyed after the June move expected December and 36% selected October.

The yen’s position near its weakest level since 1986 increased the cost of waiting, although the government’s stance remained a source of uncertainty. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has favored monetary accommodation. A revised version of the government’s economic-policy guidance included language respecting BOJ independence, but investors will examine the final document for any attempt to influence the pace of tightening.

Japan’s 3-month bill auction provided a current short-end funding result. The Ministry of Finance accepted ¥2.898 trillion of competitive bids at a weighted-average price of 99.7634, equivalent to a 0.9618% yield. The lowest accepted price was 99.7615, or 0.9695%, with 30.3121% allotted at that level. The bills are issued July 21 and mature October 19. Competitive bids totaled ¥11.572 trillion, indicating substantial demand without resolving the policy debate over the next BOJ increase.

India faced a more immediate exposure to both food and energy supply. Reserve Bank Governor Sanjay Malhotra said inflation remained elevated after exceeding the bank’s 4% target for the first time in almost 18 months. He attributed much of the pressure to supply factors but identified the Middle East conflict and a weak monsoon as the principal threats to the outlook.

India imports almost 90% of its oil, and close to half of those shipments ordinarily pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed rise in crude therefore increased the risk of broader domestic pass-through. Rainfall was 23% below its long-term average, threatening crop sowing in a country where the monsoon supplies about 70% of annual precipitation. Former Agriculture Secretary Siraj Hussain said food inflation could exceed 7%, with pulses and oilseeds particularly exposed to the distribution of rain through the end of August.

The RBI has held its policy rate at 5.25% throughout 2026 and has said it would react if price pressure broadened. Malhotra continued to describe tightening as premature and favored waiting for more evidence. The central bank also reduced its growth forecast to 6.6% from 6.9%, illustrating the cost of an oil shock for an import-dependent economy even before inflation becomes sufficiently widespread to trigger higher rates. The RBI’s next meeting is scheduled for August 3–5.

## Forward Market Significance

The ECB decision on July 23 is the first major policy test. A hold is widely expected, placing the emphasis on how President Christine Lagarde describes September. June inflation fell to 2.8%, services pressure moderated and evidence of second-round effects remained limited. Continued disruption through Hormuz would nevertheless preserve the case for another increase, while weaker activity and stabilized energy prices would reduce the need to tighten again.

The same day, the U.S. Treasury will sell $21 billion of new 10-year inflation-protected securities at 13:00 ET. The issue settles July 31 and matures July 15, 2036. The auction will test demand for real duration and explicit inflation protection after Friday’s 1.9-basis-point decline in the 10-year real yield and 1.4-basis-point rise in the breakeven rate. Oil’s further post-close advance makes the division between those components especially important.

Japan’s June national consumer-price index is due July 24. It will help determine whether the BOJ’s improved growth assessment and faster corporate cost pass-through warrant another increase as early as October or allow officials to wait until December. The result will also shape the yen and domestic demand for JGBs as investors weigh a 1% policy rate against persistent inflation above target.

UK retail sales for June arrive July 24 at 07:00 BST. Household demand will be a central constraint on Bank of England policy as Britain absorbs higher imported energy costs and a change in political leadership. Resilient consumption would leave more room to respond to inflation, while weakness would reinforce the growth cost of additional tightening.

U.S. new-home sales follow at 10:00 ET on July 24. They will provide the demand-side counterpart to Friday’s construction report. The 19% rise in starts was driven by multifamily building, while single-family starts and permits declined. Sales will indicate whether completed inventory is finding buyers or whether mortgage costs continue to restrain the part of housing most sensitive to Treasury yields.

The July 28–29 FOMC meeting remains the principal U.S. policy event. Markets have reduced the probability of an immediate increase to about 15%, and the communications blackout limits officials’ ability to reshape that expectation. The more consequential question is how Warsh characterizes the later path after nonfuel import prices rose, Hammack emphasized broad business concern about inflation, and oil erased part of June’s energy relief.

Credit execution will provide a parallel market test. San Antonio’s $944 million airport transaction is scheduled to price July 21, while Baker Tilly’s proposed $3 billion refinancing moves into investor meetings. Neuquén begins marketing its prospective $500 million international bond the same day. Their outcomes will show how much differentiation remains among long municipal duration, acquisition-backed leveraged debt and energy-supported emerging-market credit.

The decisive fixed-income issue is no longer whether one favorable inflation week removed the case for a July Fed increase. The curve and policy pricing already reflect that conclusion. The unresolved test is whether June disinflation survives a renewed oil shock while U.S. demand remains resilient and AI investment continues to support activity, costs and borrowing. Friday’s flatter Treasury curve captured that uncertainty: the long end found support from uneven growth and falling technology shares, but the front end could not dismiss a tightening cycle that has been deferred rather than conclusively ended.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury curve flattens as oil revives later Fed risk while uneven growth and a technology selloff support duration
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries ended July 17 with a bearish flattening at the front of the curve. The 2-year yield rose 3.8 basis points to 4.18%, while the 10-year slipped 0.5 basis point to 4.549% and the 30-year fell 1.3 basis points to 5.071%. The move left 2s10s 4.3 basis points flatter at 36.9 basis points as investors separated an unlikely July Fed increase from the possibility of tightening later in the year.

June import prices rose 0.3% and 7.1% from a year earlier, with nonfuel costs still firm, while renewed U.S.-Iran attacks disrupted Hormuz shipping and drove WTI and Brent roughly 4.5% higher. Those inflation risks contrasted with softer underlying activity: the 19% rise in housing starts was concentrated in multifamily construction, single-family starts and permits declined, and manufacturing output was unchanged.

That divide also appeared inside the 10-year yield. The real yield fell 1.9 basis points to 2.295% as uneven growth and a technology-led equity selloff supported duration, while the breakeven rate rose 1.4 basis points to 2.254% as energy risk rebuilt inflation compensation. Credit remained broadly available, but hyperscaler debt underperformance and Cotality's costly refinancing showed that repeated supply, leverage and weaker protections increasingly required investor concessions.
